attack_mechanism: During a CALL, jump, or instruction that writes R0, `pc_sw_wr` has priority in the `pc_nxt` multiplexer and selects `pc_sw`. A transient bit flip or forced value on `openMSP430.inst_dest` before the next `mclk` edge can substitute a false target or assert the software-write selection on the wrong instruction. `openMSP430.inst_dest` participates in forming or qualifying that software-PC path; the state and data choices on this path depend on `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.pc_sw_wr`. The corrupted target is captured in `pc`, redirecting control flow, skipping intended instructions, or executing an unintended basic block. The concrete design route is `openMSP430.inst_dest -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.pc_sw_wr -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`.

With no software PC write and no interrupt-vector state active, `pc_nxt` falls through to `pc_incr = pc + {14'h0, fetch, 1'b0}`. Injecting a transient or stuck fault into `openMSP430.inst_dest` before `pc` is enabled can add the wrong increment or prevent the expected increment. `openMSP430.inst_dest` affects `fetch`, instruction length, or the instruction-state decision used by this sequential increment; the state and data choices on this path depend on `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.src_reg_dest_sel`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.src_reg_src_sel`, `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.inst_bw`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_sw_wr`. The next instruction is skipped, repeated, or fetched from an unintended address. The concrete design route is `openMSP430.inst_dest -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_dest -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_add -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`.

Instruction fetch is released from `I_DEC` only when `exec_done` or `E_IDLE` is observed, and `e_state` also determines whether jump, source-write, or destination-write completion is pending. A fault on `openMSP430.inst_dest` can falsely complete an instruction or hold the execution machine in an earlier phase when `pc_nxt` is evaluated. `openMSP430.inst_dest` controls that execution sequencing before the frontend selects the next PC update; the state and data choices on this path depend on `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.cpuoff`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_sw_wr`. The PC is advanced too early, held too long, or updated with operands belonging to the wrong instruction phase. The concrete design route is `openMSP430.inst_dest -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r2_wr -> openMSP430.frontend_0.e_state_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.pc`.
